targetedParagraphRepairs.before: Even without reported thirst, check intake, excretion and condition changes. Around hot environments, exercise and bathing, review room temperature and opportunities for fluids according to the person’s plan.
targetedParagraphRepairs.after: Even if the person does not report thirst, check for changes in eating, drinking, excretion and physical condition. In hot surroundings and before or after exercise or bathing, review the room temperature and opportunities to take fluids according to the person’s plan.

targetedParagraphRepairs.before: With heart- or kidney-related fluid restrictions or swallowing difficulty, workers do not independently increase amounts or change methods. Report dry mouth and reduced urine for assessment and follow the individual care plan confirmed with healthcare professionals. This lesson does not establish a universal replacement-fluid amount.
targetedParagraphRepairs.after: If the person has fluid restrictions because of a heart or kidney condition, or has difficulty swallowing, care workers must not independently increase drinking amounts or change the way fluids are provided. Report a dry mouth or reduced urine output and request assessment. Follow the individual care plan confirmed with healthcare professionals. This lesson does not establish one fluid-replacement amount that applies to everyone.

targetedParagraphRepairs.before: Fiber-containing meals, suitable activity and opportunities such as after meals are considered in the individual care plan. Check swallowing ability and fluid restrictions too; do not force identical meals or timing on everyone. With fever, also confirm a suitable way to provide fluids.
targetedParagraphRepairs.after: Meals containing dietary fiber, activity suited to the person and support at times when bowel movements may be easier, such as after meals, are matters to consider in the individual care plan. For fluids, also check swallowing ability and any restrictions. Do not impose the same meals or timing on everyone. When the person has a fever, confirm a suitable method for providing fluids as well.

targetedParagraphRepairs.before: Bowel problems with persistent abdominal pain, vomiting or blood in stool should be promptly connected to healthcare professionals without waiting a set number of days. Actual support follows condition, the individual care plan and facility procedures. This lesson does not determine diagnoses or treatments.
targetedParagraphRepairs.after: If bowel problems are accompanied by persistent abdominal pain, vomiting, blood in the stool or similar concerns, promptly seek help from healthcare professionals without waiting a set number of days. Actual assistance follows the person’s condition, individual care plan and facility procedures. This lesson is not intended to determine a diagnosis or treatment method.

targetedParagraphRepairs.before: Observe swelling’s location, side, degree and change from usual. It may occur on the affected side with hemiplegia, but do not attribute every one-sided swelling to paralysis. Include planned information such as weight in the report.
targetedParagraphRepairs.after: Observe the location, side and degree of swelling and any change from the person’s usual condition. Swelling may appear on the affected side in a person with hemiplegia, but do not assume that all swelling on one side is caused by paralysis. Include information required by the plan, such as body weight, in the report.

targetedParagraphRepairs.before: Report personal words separately from observed skin. Moisturizing follows appropriate products and the plan. Coordinate with healthcare professionals for abnormalities. Do not add unknown causes to records or independently select medication or new procedures.
targetedParagraphRepairs.after: Communicate the person’s own words separately from the skin condition you have actually observed. Use moisturizing products and methods suited to the person and their plan. Coordinate with healthcare professionals if there are abnormalities. Do not add unconfirmed causes to the record or independently choose medication or a new procedure.
